# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- The routes, by name. Speech reaches Mute and Blind, and never Deaf. Gestures
  reach Deaf and Mute, and never Blind. Deaf can speak and gesture, Mute can
  only gesture, Blind can only speak. Check every message against this list
  before you send it.

- Deaf invents the gesture code out loud before anything else moves, and
  everyone else's opening move is waiting for it. The manual's verdict reaches
  Blind only as Deaf's spoken order.

- Whatever the code becomes, it starts by being able to say YES, NO, HOLD and
  DONE. Grow it only when a message will not fit.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I see a green light, display 9, and five wires: white, green, red, yellow, and purple. No manual information or physical result is available to me yet. I am establishing the required shared gesture code before anyone attempts an action: 👍 YES, 👎 NO, ✋ HOLD, and 👌 DONE. The spoken descriptions reach Blind, while the gestures reach Mute.

``` 
speak(text="Gesture code: thumbs up means YES; thumbs down means NO; raised hand means HOLD; OK hand means DONE.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged: display 9, green light, and wires ordered white, green, red, yellow, purple. I am clarifying the shared protocol and passing the full visual state to both teammates. Mute should read the manual and use the established gestures to report whether the proposed action is acceptable; Blind should wait for my spoken relay.

``` 
speak(text="Protocol confirmed: 👍 means YES, 👎 means NO, ✋ means HOLD, and 👌 means DONE. Bomb state: display 9; light green; wires in order 1 white, 2 green, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 purple. Mute, read the manual and report its verdict with the protocol gestures. Blind, wait for my spoken relay; do not act yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute sent 🤟, which is not part of the agreed code, so I cannot safely interpret it as a verdict. I am instructing Mute to resend using only the established signals, and I am telling Blind not to act until the manual’s result is clear.

``` 
speak(text="Mute, I saw 🤟, but it is not assigned. Please resend the manual verdict using only 👍 for YES, 👎 for NO, ✋ for HOLD, or 👌 for DONE. Blind, do not act yet; the manual verdict is not established.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute has sent the established HOLD signal. The bomb remains unchanged, so no physical action should be taken. I am relaying HOLD to Blind and asking Mute to continue only when the manual gives a definite instruction.

``` 
speak(text="Mute reports HOLD. Blind, HOLD: do not touch or operate anything. Mute, continue consulting the manual and report the next definite verdict using the agreed gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Both teammates are signaling HOLD, so no action is authorized. The bomb remains unchanged. I will keep the bomb on hold and ask Mute to obtain a definite manual instruction; Blind must not operate anything until that instruction is relayed.

``` 
speak(text="Both reports are HOLD. Do not touch or operate the bomb. Mute, continue reading the manual and report the next definite instruction using the agreed signals.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Mute continues to report HOLD, so there is still no safe authorization to touch the bomb. The earlier 🤟 cannot be used because it was never assigned. I am defining a compact extension: if the manual authorizes cutting, Mute should send 👍 followed by one to five additional 👍 gestures for the wire number; if it forbids or gives no cut instruction, send 👎; use ✋ only when the manual genuinely requires waiting. Blind must continue holding.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Your repeated HOLD is understood as no action yet. To report the manual precisely: send 👍 if it authorizes cutting, then one to five additional 👍 gestures for wire number 1 through 5. Send 👎 if it forbids cutting or gives no cut instruction. Use ✋ only if the manual explicitly says wait. Blind, continue HOLD; do not operate anything.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[red] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍]

Mute’s four thumbs-up gestures decode as YES plus three additional thumbs-up gestures: the manual authorizes cutting wire 3. Wire 3 is red. Blind has already had this round’s turn, so I am sending the instruction for the next round and confirming the decoded result to Mute.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Manual verdict: YES. Cut wire 3, the red wire. Do this on your next turn; do not cut any other wire.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[CUT] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The previous cut was correct, and the bomb has changed. I now see display 4, a yellow light, and remaining wires 1 white, 2 green, 4 yellow, and 5 purple; wire 3 is cut. I am relaying this new state and instructing the team to pause while Mute checks the manual.

``` 
speak(text="New bomb state after the correct cut: display 4; light yellow; wire 3 is cut; remaining wires are 1 white, 2 green, 4 yellow, and 5 purple. Mute, consult the manual for this new state. Blind, do not act until the manual verdict is relayed.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[CUT] 4:[yellow] 5:[purple]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍]

The bomb remains at display 4 with a yellow light. Mute’s six thumbs-up gestures decode as YES plus five additional thumbs-up gestures, so the manual authorizes cutting wire 5, which is purple. I am sending Blind the instruction for the next turn.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Manual verdict: YES. Cut wire 5, the purple wire. Do this on your next turn; do not cut any other wire.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[CUT] 4:[yellow] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The second cut was correct, and the bomb has changed again. I see display 3, a green light, wires 1 white, 2 green, 4 yellow, with wires 3 and 5 cut. I am sending the new state to Mute and Blind and instructing Blind not to act until Mute reads the updated manual instruction.

``` 
speak(text="New bomb state after the correct cut: display 3; light green; wire 3 is cut; wire 5 is cut; remaining wires are 1 white, 2 green, and 4 yellow. Mute, consult the manual for this state. Blind, do not act until the manual verdict is relayed.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✋"])
wait()
```

Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]

Mute’s two thumbs-up gestures mean YES plus one additional thumbs-up: the manual authorizes cutting wire 1, the white wire. I am relaying that instruction to Blind for the next turn; no other wire should be touched.

